clue.text: Plant about to be attached to decoration

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for concerning, as in a letter heading
finery is showy ornament or dress

explanation.surface: A garden plant is about to have an ornament tied on to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks botanical but means an industrial works; 'to be attached to' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial works where crude materials such as oil or sugar are purified is a kind of factory plant.

clue.text: Tune for a film in 1990

parts.note: the two words for and tune, written the other way round, give these two clue words, so the instruction to turn them describes the clue

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a tune to accompany a film released in 1990.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, swaps the order of FOR and TUNE, giving 'Tune for'. The film is Barbet Schroeder's 1990 drama about Claus von Bülow.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1990 courtroom drama starring Jeremy Irons as Claus von Bülow bears this title.

clue.text: See 1
Ultimately turn you on? One hopes not

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A question about whether something will arouse you, answered with the hope that it will not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' picks the last letters of turn, you and on. The definition is a joke: a woman under vows of chastity hopes not to be turned on.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a religious order under a vow of celibacy would hope never to be aroused.

clue.text: Irritable dog worried merchant near here?

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered dog has upset a trader in the vicinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges IRRITABLE DOG. The merchant is Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, and this Venetian bridge was the city's commercial centre, so he would trade near here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice does business on the Rialto, the trading district round this famous Venetian bridge.

clue.text: Stand beneath soldier's intended destination

parts.note: a soldier here is a finger of toast meant to be dipped into a boiled egg, and the holder sits underneath that egg

explanation.surface: Military orders about where an infantryman should stand when he arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'soldier' is British slang for a strip of toast dunked into a soft-boiled egg; the small stand holds the egg it is aimed at.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds a boiled egg upright, the target into which toast fingers are dipped at breakfast.

clue.text: Work around former underworld to drum up financial incentive

indicators.note: around tells us the word for work wraps itself about the other pieces

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine goes
olden means of former times
hell is the underworld of the dead

explanation.surface: Hard labour in the old underworld is used to raise money as an inducement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' splits the word for work to hold the other two pieces. A golden hello is a lump sum paid to a new recruit, used to drum up staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off payment offered to someone for joining a firm is a lure to recruit them.

clue.text: Man almost finds endless happiness in wine

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for man is dropped

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: endless means the word for happiness loses its final letter

parts.note: bliss is perfect happiness

explanation.surface: A fellow nearly finds unbounded joy in a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CHAP to CHA and 'endless' trims BLISS to BLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white Burgundy from the town of Chablis is a well-known wine.

clue.text: Heroin discovered in seat-what a relief

indicators.note: found within, so the letter for the drug sits inside the word for a seat

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in church
H is slang shorthand for heroin

explanation.surface: Drugs found hidden in a church bench, and someone sighs with relief.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses relief after strain or a narrow escape.

clue.text: Queen visiting a museum's horse gallery

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so the monarch's letters go inside the museum

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
horse is slang for heroin, which is abbreviated H

explanation.surface: The Queen calls in on a museum to view its horse gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' puts ER inside V AND A, the Victoria and Albert Museum; H follows. 'Horse' is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: An open roofed gallery along the side of a house is this kind of porch.

clue.text: Does she use money borrowed in the London area?

definitions.text: Does she use money borrowed in the London area?

indicators.note: in tells us the borrowed money sits inside the London district

parts.note: SE is a London postal area, south-east
a loan is money borrowed

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman lives on credit in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a well-heeled young woman of London's Sloane Square set, so she plausibly spends borrowed money there; SE is the south-east London postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane Ranger is a wealthy, fashionable young woman from the Chelsea set around Sloane Square in London.

clue.text: One with glitz lost in no-man's-land?

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone glamorous gets lost in a stretch of disputed ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges ONE WITH GLITZ. The definition is a hazy, indeterminate state, like the sci-fi TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: An indeterminate state between two conditions, belonging to neither, is like an unclaimed border strip.

clue.text: Turner painted in green, red and black

definitions.text: Turner painted in green, red and black

parts.words: Turner painted in green, red and black
parts.note: not the painter but something that turns, a spinning casino device coloured with green, red and black pockets

explanation.surface: Describes a canvas by the painter J.M.W. Turner in three colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the landscape painter, but here it is anything that spins: the casino's spinning disc has red and black numbered slots and a green zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino gambling device spins, and its pockets are coloured red and black with a green zero.

clue.text: Forecast to catch nothing on line cast regularly in a river

indicators.note: in says the pieces before it go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to trap is to catch
O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of cast, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: An angler predicts a blank after casting a line at intervals in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of cast; 'in' puts the four pieces inside a Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: To project a trend beyond known data is to predict or estimate future values.

clue.text: Something from field's left in rubbish skip

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: tripe is nonsense or rubbish
to skip is to jump

explanation.surface: Something from a field has been dumped in a rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' is athletics field events, not farmland, and 'skip' is a verb (jump), not a British rubbish container. The 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hop, step and jump is an athletics field event, contested away from the running track.

clue.text: Cause colour to fade away at the edges

indicators.text: to fade away at the edges
indicators.note: fading at the edges means the first and last letters of the colour vanish

parts.note: magenta is a purplish-red colour

explanation.surface: A reason why a colour fades round the borders of a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fade away at the edges' drops the first and last letters of MAGENTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is something that brings about an effect, a means or instigator.

clue.text: Wise guy using a key has entered into pub

indicators.note: entered into means gone inside, so the other pieces sit within the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever fellow uses a key to get into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise guy' is not a smart alec but one of the Three Wise Men; ALT, HAS and A go 'into' BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Balthasar is traditionally named as one of the three Magi, the Wise Men of the Nativity.

clue.text: Shocking exposure about the cloth

indicators.note: about means the word for exposure is placed round the cloth

parts.note: outing is public exposure of someone's secret
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A scandalous exposure involving the clergy, the cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' suggests the clergy but here is just a scrap of fabric; 'about' wraps the exposure round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outraging means offending gravely, as shocking behaviour does.

clue.text: Moon I associated with a different one

parts.note: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn

explanation.surface: An astronomer links one moon with another.
explanation.walkthrough: TITAN, I and A combine; the result is a different moon, the largest satellite of Uranus.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, so another moon besides Saturn's Titan.

clue.text: Hammered rim around semi-cylinder

indicators.note: around means the word for rim goes outside the half-word

parts.note: a lip is a rim or edge
a cylinder is a tube, and the first half of that word gives the semi part

explanation.surface: A metal rim beaten round a half-pipe shape.
explanation.walkthrough: TU is the first half ('semi') of TUBE, a cylinder. 'Hammered' means drunk, not beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drunk is colloquially described as being illuminated, the slang sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Coach missing the point in hackneyed praise

indicators.note: in puts the shortened vehicle inside the word for hackneyed

parts.note: trite means hackneyed or overused

indicators.note: missing means the compass letter is taken out of the coach

parts.note: a bus is a coach
S is a point of the compass, south

explanation.surface: A coach misses the point in some stale words of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes S, a compass point, from BUS, leaving BU, which goes 'in' TRITE. 'Coach' means a vehicle, not a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an act or statement of homage, expressing admiration.

clue.text: Blair's secret service

parts.note: Blair here is Eric Blair, the novelist known as George Orwell, and his secret service punishes forbidden ideas in Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.surface: A reference to Prime Minister Tony Blair's intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony Blair, but it is Eric Blair, George Orwell's real name; in his novel Nineteen Eighty-Four this force hunts down dissident ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four features a secret force punishing unorthodox ideas.

clue.text: Cross fellow failing to finish short holiday

annotationWithheld.why: 'Cross fellow failing to finish short holiday' (4) for XMAS: X (cross) leaves MAS, but no fellow word trimmed of its end gives MAS as held (MA from MAN wants a possessive 's, perhaps lost in OCR); no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Cross fellow failing to finish short holiday

clue.text: Servant oddly unable to find guide

parts.note: a man is a manservant

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of unable, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A servant, strangely incapable, tries to find a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes UAL from UnAbLe.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual is a handbook of instructions, a guide.

clue.text: Capital's still short in most of credit

indicators.note: in puts the shortened calm inside the shortened credit
most of drops the last letter of the word for credit

parts.note: honour is credit, as in a credit to the school

indicators.note: short means the word for a quiet period loses its last letter

parts.note: a lull is a still, a period of calm

explanation.surface: A city is still short of money, most of its credit gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts HONOUR to HONOU; 'short' cuts LULL to LUL, which goes 'in' it. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the state capital of Hawaii.

clue.text: Poorly scientist drops container

indicators.note: drops means the container's letters are taken out of the scientist

parts.note: a boffin is a scientist, especially a research one
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: An unwell scientist drops a container.
explanation.walkthrough: BOFFIN is British slang for a scientist; take out B and IN to leave OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off is feeling unwell or below par.

clue.text: Mum has to maintain youngster

parts.note: mum as in keep mum, be quiet, which the command sh asks for
to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: A mother has to support her child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but silence, as in 'keep mum'; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A young shaver is an old colloquial term for a boy or young lad.

clue.text: DIY shelf fixed with some panel pins

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of repaired or put right, so these letters are reordered
some means only part of the words panel pins is taken

explanation.surface: Doing it yourself: putting up a shelf with a few panel pins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges SHELF to SELFH and 'some' takes ELP from panEL Pins. Panel pins are small thin nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-it-yourself is improving matters by one's own efforts rather than relying on others.
